---
title: "KV Cache"
description: "A memory structure that stores recent key and value activations for efficient autoregressive generation."
term: "KV Cache"
letter: "K"
category: "Inference Systems"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

A KV cache stores the key and value vectors computed for earlier tokens in a
sequence so the model does not need to recalculate them every time it generates
a new token. It is a common optimization in large language models.

## Technical explanation

During autoregressive generation, a transformer processes tokens one by one.
For each layer, the model computes key and value vectors for the current token.
Rather than recomputing all previous keys and values at every step, inference
systems store them in a cache and append new ones as generation proceeds. This
reduces repeated computation and improves throughput.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

KV caching is essential for efficient serving of LLMs. Without it, generating a
long response would repeatedly reprocess the entire prompt, increasing time and
cost. The cache is also a major factor in memory usage during inference.

## How it works

When a sequence is processed, each transformer layer stores its computed keys
and values for that sequence. As the model continues generating, it reads the
cached keys and values for prior tokens and only computes the new token's key
and value. The model then performs attention over the combined set.

## Practical example

A chat model receives a long prompt and then generates a long answer token by
token. The KV cache holds the intermediate attention context from earlier tokens,
so later tokens can attend to the whole prompt without recomputing everything
from scratch.

## Common misconceptions

- KV cache is not a database; it is a temporary inference optimization.
- It is not the same as storing the whole conversation history in a human-readable form.
- Larger caches can improve speed but consume more memory and must be managed carefully.
